tfn.s: Japan has a word for death caused by working too much.
tfn.why: The text says: "karoshi", which means death from overwork.

tfn.s: The government has removed all legal limits on overtime.
tfn.why: The text says the change "was not the same as removing all legal limits".

tfn.s: More workers in the survey wanted to work fewer hours than wanted to work more.
tfn.why: The text says 30% wanted fewer hours and about 11% wanted more.

tfn.s: The survey asked workers how much money they earn.

tfn.s: The text says a shorter working day always makes people happier.
tfn.why: The text says a shorter day "is not automatically a happier one".

tfn.s: In September 2026 Japan removed all legal limits on overtime.
tfn.why: The text says existing legal protections "were not simply abolished".

tfn.s: Fewer than half of the surveyed workers wanted to change their hours.
tfn.why: About 30% wanted fewer hours and one in ten wanted more, and "Most were satisfied".

tfn.s: The labour shortage affects only the care sector.
tfn.why: The text says it affects sectors "ranging from care services to manufacturing".

tfn.s: The survey was carried out in Tokyo.
tfn.why: The text does not say where the survey was carried out.

tfn.s: Tokyo's government has made a four-day week compulsory for every company in Japan.
tfn.why: The text says the option is for eligible staff and "it is not a national requirement".

focus.note: Learn each verb or adjective with its preposition as one chunk, and check it in a dictionary.

items.s: Managers should be held accountable ____ the health of their teams.

Campaigners warned that the reforms would be ____ by so many exemptions that they would achieve very little.
Employers who breach their ____ duties, such as paying the minimum wage, can be fined.

Without more workers, the country may be unable to ____ its pension system for decades.

items.s: Campaigners have called for greater ____ about how overtime is recorded.

tfn.s: The labour ministry's 2026 change removed the legal ceiling on overtime.
tfn.why: The text calls it "a change in guidance, not a wholesale abolition of statutory overtime protections".

tfn.s: The survey found nearly three times as many workers wanting fewer hours as wanting more.
tfn.why: The text gives 30% for fewer hours against 10.5% for more.

tfn.s: The text suggests that a four-day week always reduces an employee's workload.
tfn.why: The text says "a four-day schedule does not necessarily mean a four-day workload".

tfn.s: The labour ministry plans to restore the 45-hour recommendation next year.
tfn.why: The text says nothing about the ministry's future plans.

tfn.s: The text suggests that one overtime policy can feel like freedom to one employee and pressure to another.
tfn.why: One worker wanting extra income may find limits frustrating, while an anxious colleague "may experience the same supposed freedom as pressure".

focus.note: Formal phrases like these are fixed chunks. Learn the whole phrase, not the preposition alone.

speak.title: Role-play: can I leave on time?
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Your employee wants to leave at five every day. The team is busy and you often stay late yourself. Ask at least two questions before you decide. You can say yes, no, or yes with a condition.

b.text: You finish your work by five, but nobody leaves before the manager. Ask to leave on time. Explain why it matters to you and how you will keep the work up to date.

phrases: I was hoping to leave at five every day.
I've finished everything on my list.
Are you worried about how it looks?
I'd be happy to try it for a month.
I'm afraid we can't, because we're short of staff.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: did the manager say yes, and was it a fair decision?
